newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crude interest perks, Forcados to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crude interest perks, Forcados to Gulf.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude business featured talk of heavy buying of North Sea Forties barrels on Tuesday, and the sale of a Nigerian Forcados cargo to a refiner in the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
An end-December Forcados was heard sold to an unnamed U.S. Gulf refiner at dated Brent plus 75 cents.
"It looks like it is surely coming into the Gulf," said a trader.

Forties was sold for January 5-7 at dated Brent plus 28 cents, more in line with what the market gauged the current value. Monday saw a Forties sale at dated plus 18 cents, down sharply from previous levels above the dated plus 35-41 cents mark.
U.S. traders also talked, but could not confirm, that a major Wall Street refiner bought a January 1-3 Brent cargo from a U.K. major at January Brent minus 13 cents.
The last confirmed Brent sale was at January Brent minus 12 cents, and involved the same Wall Street refiner.
In the U.S. aftermarket window, paper Brent dealings were called thin with only four partial trades.

Against an IPE February Brent settlement Tuesday at $23.70, a total of one full cargo was sold. A Wall Street broker bought 200 lots at $23.75 and 200 more lots at $23.73. A further 100 lots were sold at $23.70 in a separate deal.
One January/February Brent spread was dealt at plus 52 cents, 5 cents higher than during the London session.
Action in London time focused on the weakness in dated Brent and Forties.
One Brent cargo was kept voluntarily and a second was left unclaimed. British Petroleum kept a January 1-3 cargo and Esso was clocked with a parcel in the same period.
